text:
maya: CI turned red on main after the lockfile regen PR (4321). ubuntu/py310 unit tests failing, looks consistent across runs.
ci-bot: Build failed: GH Actions job 'unit-tests' (ubuntu-22.04). Failing test: tests/test_http_parsing.py::test_content_type - AssertionError
```
  E   AssertionError: expected 'application/json; charset=utf-8' got None
  tests/test_http_parsing.py:42: in test_content_type
    assert parse_content_type(headers) == 'application/json; charset=utf-8'
```
sam: I grabbed the full log. Stack points into our url/header parsing lib — there was a transitive bump in one of the deps during lock regen. Could be rfc parsing behavior change.
jordan: Can someone try to repro locally with the same lockfile? `git checkout def456 && poetry install --no-dev && tox -e py310` — if you can reproduce we can bisect. I can run the git bisect if someone gives the bad/good commits.
maya: Reproduced locally following those steps. Fails on that exact assertion. On the commit before lock regen (abc123) the test passes. So it's definitely introduced by the lockfile changes, not our test code.
alex: Quick try: pinning the transitive `rfc3986` back to the previous patch helped locally for me (`poetry add rfc3986@^1.4.0 --lock`). Not a long-term fix but gives a place to start.
priya: I'll kick a bisect and/or rerun CI with selective pin to confirm. @jordan can you paste the lockfile commit hash? Also I've requested a GH workflow rerun.
ci-bot: ci: workflow rerun requested by @priya - https://github.com/redwood-inference/repo/actions/runs/987654321
jordan: Bisect started. Range abc123..def456 (def456 is the lock regen). First bad commit points to the dependency set that includes rfc3986 1.5.1 (was 1.4.0). Opening a tiny PR to pin rfc3986 to 1.4.x in the lock to unblock CI.
maya: For safety, can we add a small defensive change in parse_content_type to handle the None case and log the header? I'll make a follow-up PR if the pin is accepted.
sam: Sounds good. If the pin PR passes CI I'll merge and then we can follow up upstream with rfc3986 or adjust our parsing accordingly.
priya: Thanks all — will monitor the rerun and the bisect PR. If anyone hits this locally and wants to help test the pin, comment on the PR. :thumbsup:
